sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from $4,860.4m in FY2016 to $14,342.9m in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198].
The path was not smooth: revenue jumped 89.1% in FY2021 to $16,071.7m, then fell 24.3% in FY2022 to $12,172.9m [F6][F7][D241][D292].
REGEN-COV contributed 66.4pp of growth and 36.3% of revenue in FY2021, then fell to zero in FY2022 [D582][D580][S49][D585].
Since FY2022 revenue has grown at only a 5.6% three-year CAGR, and FY2025 added just 1.0% [D767][D440].
Net product sales fell 17.3% in FY2025 and subtracted 9.3pp from growth, while collaboration revenue rose 21.0% and added 9.0pp [D506][D507][D522][D523].
US EYLEA sales dropped 42.4% to $2,747.8m on competitive pressure, compounded bevacizumab, the EYLEA HD transition and a lower net selling price [S43][D577][P10].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits rose 33.6% to $5,241.6m, driven by higher Dupixent sales [S52][D591][P9].
That share reached 36.5% of revenue in FY2025, making it the largest single driver [D590].
Operating income fell 10.3% against 1.0% revenue growth, so incremental margin was negative and operating costs grew 4.4pp faster than revenue [D441][D440][D464].
Operating margin of 24.9% in FY2025 is the window low, 9.7pp below the 34.6% median and 30.8pp below the 55.7% FY2021 high [F30][D749][D751][D750].
R&D took 4.7pp off margin as it rose 14.0% to $5,850.2m, or 40.8% of revenue [D465][D455][X34][D420].
SG&A added 2.0pp back, falling 8.6% to $2,700.0m primarily on lower charitable contributions to Good Days [D466][D456][X47][P5].
Gross margin on net product sales also fell on manufacturing investment, higher inventory write-offs and higher Libtayo amortization [P4].
Net margin of 31.4% exceeded operating margin by 6.5pp, helped by $1,652.8m of other income and a 13.9% tax rate [F50][F30][D797][X117][D427].
Operating cash flow of $4,978.9m was 1.11x net income, and free cash flow of $4,080.5m was 0.91x, against a 0.88x window median [F80][F40][D428][F100][D429][D763].
Free cash flow margin of 28.4% sits above the 26.4% median but well below the 40.6% FY2021 high [D425][D757][D756].
Capex rose 18.9% to $898.4m, 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A [D447][F90][D424][D430].
The FY2021 receivables build came from REGEN-COV sales to the US government, and its FY2022 collection lifted that year's conversion [P20].
Net cash reached $16,879.9m, or 117.7% of revenue, the 100th percentile of eight biopharma peers against a -50.7% median [D434][D435][D780][D781].
Debt is a flat $1,985.9m and the current ratio is 4.13x [F187][F180].
Buybacks and dividends of $3,808.9m absorbed 93.3% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D436][D437][D459].
Return on average equity of 14.9% ranks in the 25th percentile against a 38.7% peer median [D439][D784][D785].
Operating margin has fallen four straight years, 30.7pp from 55.7% in FY2021 to 24.9% in FY2025, and now sits at the window low [R1][F26][F30][D749].
The decline is structural: EYLEA US sales fell from $6,264.6m in FY2022 to $2,747.8m in FY2025 on competitive pressure and the HD transition [S40][S43][P10].
The table's FY2018 revenue of $5,145.6m and FY2019 of $6,557.6m are recasts against $6,710.8m and $7,863.4m first reported, so growth spanning those years mixes presentations [R2][F3][X3][F4][X4].
Free cash flow conversion of 0.91x trails the 1.11x peer median, ranking 29th percentile [D429][D783][D782].
If FY2026 operating margin stays below the 24.9% FY2025 low, the four-year decline has not reversed; a move back toward the 34.6% median would break it [F30][D749][D751].
Watch US EYLEA sales against the $2,747.8m FY2025 level; further declines would keep subtracting from growth as they did at -14.2pp [S43][D578].
Watch R&D as a share of revenue against 40.8%; a move back toward the 34.6% median would restore operating leverage [D420][D760].
